CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this package does

auk is an R package that acts as a front end to the Unix utility AWK for extracting and processing subsets of the eBird Basic Dataset (EBD) — a very large (tens to hundreds of GB) tab-separated text file of bird observation records. R itself is only used to build and validate filters; the actual row filtering of the full dataset is done by generating and running an AWK script, since reading the whole file into R is impractical.

Common commands

Development workflow is driven from makefile.R (not a real Makefile — an R script meant to be run line-by-line in an R session):

devtools::document()        # regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE from roxygen comments
devtools::test()             # run the full test suite
devtools::check()            # full R CMD check
pkgdown::build_site()        # rebuild the pkgdown site in docs/
devtools::build_readme()     # regenerate README.md from README.Rmd

Run a single test file from an R session in the package root:

testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test_auk-filter.r")

Run a single test_that() block by temporarily adding only_test = "..." or simply isolating it — there is no CLI equivalent to devtools::test() for a single test name; use devtools::load_all() then call the test file’s contents directly, or filter with devtools::test(filter = "filter") (matches test file names, e.g. test_auk-filter.r).

After changing any roxygen2 (#') comment, re-run devtools::document() — man/*.Rd and NAMESPACE are generated files, don’t hand-edit them.

Formatting and linting — always run these

  • After writing or editing any file in R/, run air format R/. The repo’s air.toml scopes formatting to R/ only, so air format . is also safe to run from the repo root.
  • After writing or editing any file in R/, run jarl check R/ (or jarl check . — jarl.toml restricts it to R/ regardless). Fix obvious/auto-fixable issues with jarl check --fix R/ (add --allow-dirty if the working tree already has unrelated uncommitted changes). For warnings that require judgment, use judgment rather than blindly forcing a fix.
  • Do this on every change, not just when explicitly asked to format or lint.
  • Never run air/jarl over tests/, data-raw/, inst/, or makefile.R — those are intentionally out of scope per air.toml / jarl.toml.

Pipe operator

auk uses the native pipe |> exclusively — in code, docs, tests, vignettes, and maintainer scripts. There is no magrittr %>% anywhere in the package: the old auk::%>% re-export (R/pipe.R) and the magrittr dependency were both removed, so this is a breaking change for any downstream code still relying on auk’s re-exported %>%. DESCRIPTION requires R (>= 4.1.0) to support |>. Avoid the _ placeholder (which needs R >= 4.2 and only binds to a single named argument) — for the rare case where the pipe target isn’t the first argument, use an intermediate named variable instead (consistent with the general preference below against pipes in function bodies).

Architecture

The filter pipeline

auk implements a pipeline/builder pattern around two S3 classes:

  • auk_ebd (R/auk-ebd.R) — created by auk_ebd(file, file_sampling). On construction it reads just the header row of the EBD (and, if given, the associated sampling event file) to validate that required columns are present and to build col_idx / col_idx_sampling: data frames mapping canonical filter ids (e.g. "species", "country", "bcr") to the column name and 1-based column index in that specific file. Column indices matter because AWK scripts reference columns positionally ($12), and column order/presence varies between EBD file versions and custom downloads.
  • auk_sampling (R/auk-sampling.R) — same idea, but for a checklist-only (sampling event) file with no species-level filters.

Each auk_*() filter function (auk_species, auk_country, auk_state, auk_county, auk_bcr, auk_bbox, auk_date, auk_last_edited, auk_protocol, auk_project, auk_time, auk_duration, auk_distance, auk_breeding, auk_complete, auk_exotic, auk_observer, auk_year) is an S3 generic dispatching on auk_ebd/auk_sampling. Each one validates its input (e.g. species names checked against the bundled ebird_taxonomy data, countries via the countrycode package, states via ebird_states) and writes the validated value into x$filters[[...]], then returns the same object — this is what allows chaining with |>. No actual file I/O happens at this stage.

auk_filter() (R/auk-filter.R) is where filters become reality:

  1. awk_translate() walks x$filters and, for each non-empty filter, builds an AWK condition string (membership in a split()-built array for list filters like species/country/state/county/observer; numeric or string comparisons for ranges like date/time/duration/bbox) and substitutes them into the awk_filter script template using the package’s own str_interp() (${var}-style interpolation, not glue/stringr).
  2. The assembled AWK script is optionally written to awk_file.
  3. system2(awk_path, ...) executes the script against x$file (and x$file_sampling if present) via a shell call, writing output to file/file_sampling. The auk_ebd object is returned with output/output_sampling populated with the result paths.

When both an EBD and a sampling file are present, auk_filter.auk_ebd() builds and runs two AWK scripts so the two output files stay in sync — with the species/breeding/exotic filters stripped out for the sampling script (checklists aren’t species-specific) and the observer filter’s obsr prefix rewritten to obs (the sampling file uses different ID prefixes for observers).

AWK location

auk_get_awk_path()/auk_set_awk_path() (R/auk-get-awk-path.R, R/auk-set-awk-path.R) resolve the AWK binary, with special-casing for Windows/Cygwin (expects C:/cygwin/bin/gawk.exe or C:/cygwin64/...) since Windows has no AWK by default.

Reading and post-processing

  • read_ebd() / read_sampling() (R/read.R) read the AWK-filtered text output back into R with readr, applying correct column types via get_col_types() (R/utils.R) and renaming columns to snake_case.
  • auk_unique() (R/auk-unique.R) collapses duplicate group checklists (shared checklists reported by multiple observers in a group).
  • auk_rollup() (R/auk-rollup.R) rolls taxonomic reports up to species level (e.g. combining subspecies/forms, dropping “spuhs” if requested).
  • auk_zerofill() (R/auk-zerofill.R) combines a filtered EBD with its matching sampling event file to infer absences, producing an auk_zerofill object (list(observations, sampling_events), joinable on checklist_id) or, with collapse = TRUE, a single flattened data frame via collapse_zerofill().
  • format_unmarked_occu() (R/format-unmarked-occu.R) reshapes zero-filled data into the wide format expected by the unmarked package for occupancy modeling.

Taxonomy data

ebird_taxonomy, bcr_codes, ebird_states, and valid_protocols are bundled data/*.rda objects, built/updated from data-raw/*.R scripts. Filters that reference species, BCRs, states, or protocols validate against these tables rather than hitting the network. auk_species() and auk_zerofill() accept a taxonomy_version argument — if it mismatches the EBD file (detected via auk_ebd_version()/filename conventions) a warning is raised, since species name resolution depends on taxonomy version. get_ebird_taxonomy() (R/get-ebird-taxonomy.R) can fetch a specific year’s taxonomy from the eBird API when the bundled version doesn’t match.

Testing notes

  • Tests live in tests/testthat/; most existing files use the historical .r extension (test_auk-filter.r) rather than .R — match whichever extension a given file already uses; new test files should use .R per the user’s global style.
  • tests/testthat/setup.R creates a shared temp_dir under tempdir() and preserves/restores R_ENVIRON_USER and EBD_PATH env vars around the whole run.
  • Most filter/IO tests use the bundled sample data in inst/extdata/ (ebd-sample.txt, zerofill-ex_ebd.txt, zerofill-ex_sampling.txt, ebd-rollup-ex.txt, barchart-sample.txt) rather than real/full EBD files.
  • Tests that invoke AWK are skipped on CRAN and on Windows (skip_on_cran(), skip_on_os("windows")) since AWK isn’t guaranteed to be installed/configured in those environments.
  • CI (.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml) runs on macOS, Windows, and multiple Ubuntu/R version combinations.
